desc:
The string s consists of lowercase letters. The vowels are a, e, i, o, u; all other letters are consonants.

Return the number of substrings that contain every vowel at least once and exactly k consonants. Substrings are counted by position.

s = "ieaouqqieaouqq", k = 1
qualifying: s[0..5] = "ieaouq", s[6..11] = "qieaou", s[7..12] = "ieaouq"
result = 3
constraints: s contains only lowercase English letters
hints: Two conditions at once: all five vowels present, and the consonant count is exactly k. Handle them one at a time.
Let g(k) be the number of substrings with all five vowels and at least k consonants. Such substrings stay valid when extended in either direction.
The answer is g(k) - g(k + 1). Compute g with two pointers: for each right end, advance left while the window is still valid, then add left (all earlier starts are valid).
editorial: Define g(m) as the number of substrings that contain all five vowels and at least m consonants. A substring with exactly k consonants is counted by g(k) but not by g(k + 1), and every substring counted by g(k + 1) is also counted by g(k). So the answer is g(k) - g(k + 1).

Both requirements ("all vowels", "consonants ≥ m") are preserved when a substring grows. So for a fixed right end the valid starts are a prefix 0..t of the starts. Keep a window [left, right]; while it is still valid, remove s[left] (updating the vowel counts and the consonant count) and move left forward. When the loop ends, the starts 0..left-1 each gave a valid substring ending at right, so add left.
Two linear passes with O(1) memory (five vowel counters). Time O(n), space O(1).
